=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- docs/plans/pipeline-human-wait-elimination-plan.md:364-377 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Phase 10 defines a complete compare listing by total_commits <= 250 with one GET per compare, but never requires pagination or a listed-versus-total check, so a page can hold fewer commits than total_commits.
  WHY: A literal implementation would classify only part of the sync range and accept a stale merge ref; the 32-GET budget would also be too low. Severity is MAJOR in all three reports, mapped here to high. The z-ai_glm-5_3-flash adjudication disputes the finding and says the compare endpoint does not paginate.
- docs/plans/pipeline-human-wait-elimination-plan.md:103,210 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The Goal bullet (about line 103) and the Phase 10 "Done" line (about line 210) say the base is behind only by sync merges, but D10 and condition 2 also accept [ai-merge-resolve] commits, merge or not.
  WHY: A test author using Done or the Goal as the acceptance criterion would write tests that contradict condition 2. Severity is NIT in all four reports, mapped here to low.
- docs/plans/pipeline-human-wait-elimination-plan.md:381-396 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The Phase 10 step 3 Cases list has no test for a non-main default-branch sync subject, a non-merge [ai-merge-resolve] commit, or a truncated second compare.
  WHY: An implementation with a hard-coded main subject, a resolver-commit filter requiring two parents, or a first-compare-only truncation check would pass every listed case. Severity differs between reviewers: minimax_minimax-m3 says MAJOR, and the other three say NIT. The highest is used, mapped here to medium.
- docs/plans/pipeline-human-wait-elimination-plan.md:391 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The 32-GET ceiling is inconsistent with the file-listing pagination plus any compare pagination.
  WHY: An implementer could hit 33 or 34 GETs and treat the ceiling as advisory. Severity is NIT in the source, mapped here to low.
- scripts/ci_final_merge_ref_fresh.sh:181 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: CI jobs lint (135074043057) and static-checks (135066148215) stopped at the freshness guard with outcome=stale reason=not_refreshed, with tested_base 7ab9c018 and tip 0304472b.
  WHY: The failure comes from the existing guard and not from the docs content, so no edit to the plan clears it. The anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 report rates it MAJOR, while z-ai_glm-5_3-flash and minimax_minimax-m3 treat it as environmental and not a defect. MAJOR is mapped here to medium.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- docs/plans/pipeline-human-wait-elimination-plan.md:364-367 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The plan defines a complete listing by total_commits <= 250 and budgets one GET per compare, but never says to page the compare or to check that the listed commits equal total_commits.
  WHY: An implementer following the plan literally would classify only the listed commits for both compares and accept a stale merge ref after checking part of the range. The 32-GET budget would also be too low.
- docs/plans/pipeline-human-wait-elimination-plan.md:381-396 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The Cases list has no test for the default-branch-aware sync subject, for non-merge [ai-merge-resolve] commits, or for a truncated second compare.
  WHY: An implementation with a hard-coded main subject, one that rejects non-merge resolver commits, or one that checks only the first compare would pass every listed case.
- docs/plans/pipeline-human-wait-elimination-plan.md:103,210 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The Goal and the Phase 10 "Done" line still say integration-sync merges only, although D10 and condition 2 accept [ai-merge-resolve] commits, merge or not.
  WHY: A test author using Done or the Goal as the acceptance criterion would write tests that contradict condition 2.
- scripts/ci_final_merge_ref_fresh.sh (not changed by this PR), CI jobs lint (135074043057) and static-checks (135066148215) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Both jobs stopped at the freshness guard before running any checks, because the merge ref still merges into 7ab9c018 after 6 refresh attempts while main is at 0304472b.
  WHY: The failure comes from the existing guard and not from the docs content, and it clears only when the head is synced to the current main tip and a new final run starts.
- HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS: add one sentence in Phase 10 step 1, condition 1, requiring per_page=100 with pagination or a len(commits) == total_commits check that fails as detail=truncated, and raise the API budget to match (about 2 lines). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1.
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- docs/plans/pipeline-human-wait-elimination-plan.md:364-377 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Completeness is defined by total_commits <= 250 and files under 300 with one GET per compare, but the compare endpoint pages both commits and files, so a page can hold fewer entries than total_commits.
  WHY: A literal implementation classifies only the first page of a long sync range, such as 30 of 45 commits, and accepts a stale merge ref after testing part of the range.
- docs/plans/pipeline-human-wait-elimination-plan.md:103,210 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The Goal and Done descriptions say the base is behind only by sync merges, contradicting D10 and condition 2 (lines 83-87 and 366), which accept [ai-merge-resolve] commits.
  WHY: A test author reading Done as the acceptance criterion would write a test that contradicts the condition 2 behavior.
- docs/plans/pipeline-human-wait-elimination-plan.md:381-396 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The Cases list lacks cases for a non-main default branch in the sync subject, a non-merge [ai-merge-resolve] commit, and a truncated second compare.
  WHY: An implementation with a hard-coded main subject or a first-compare-only check would pass every listed test.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- docs/plans/pipeline-human-wait-elimination-plan.md:364-368,391 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Condition 1 declares the listing complete when total_commits <= 250, but the plan never says how to read all listed commits. The compare endpoint pages at a default of 30 per page, and the API budget mentions pagination only for the PR files listing.
  WHY: A literal implementation either classifies only the first page of commits and accepts a stale merge ref after testing part of the range, or uses an unjustified per_page. The 32-GET budget is also too low.
- docs/plans/pipeline-human-wait-elimination-plan.md:103,210 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The Goal and Done describe the accepted range as integration-sync merges only, but D10 (lines 83-87) and condition 2 (lines 366-368) also accept [ai-merge-resolve] commits, merge or not.
  WHY: A test author reading Done or the Goal would write tests that contradict condition 2, for example one asserting detail=foreign_commit for a non-merge resolver commit.
- docs/plans/pipeline-human-wait-elimination-plan.md:381-396 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The Cases list has no case for a non-main default branch, a non-merge [ai-merge-resolve] commit, or a truncated second compare. The "truncated compare fails" case covers only the first compare.
  WHY: A regression that hard-codes main, rejects single-parent [ai-merge-resolve] commits, or uses a partial default-branch listing would pass every listed test.
- docs/plans/pipeline-human-wait-elimination-plan.md:391 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The 32-GET ceiling is inconsistent with the file-listing pagination and with the compare pagination required by condition 1.
  WHY: An implementer hitting 33 or 34 GETs would skip a check or treat the ceiling as advisory.
- TASK_GAP (no gap raised): the reviewer confirms every deliverable in the PR descriptio
